title: Habib by a Hair: Habibsters Edge Philly by 1.12, HULK Flattens Z², and the Packers Score Everywhere but the Starting Lineups
dek: Kaushal's four-game heater survives a 132-point punch from Team Pillbert, No Banner only HULK drops the week's top score, and Week 9 turns into a festival of bench points nobody got to use.
body: The game of the week came down to the decimals. Habibsters beat Team Pillbert 133.5 to 132.38, a 1.12-point escape for a team Luffy gave only a 40% chance on Sunday morning. Puka Nacua went Gear 5, landing exactly on his 28-point top line, and CeeDee Lamb added 28.5 on a 17.68 projection, giving Habib two receivers who each outscored some lineups' entire flex spot. Jahmyr Gibbs, the swing player on Philly's side, put up 13.4, not bad and not enough. That's four straight wins for Habibsters, who have climbed from 1-4 to 5-4 and look nothing like the team that started the season tripping over its own shoelaces.

Philly will want to frame this one as a moral victory, and honestly, he'd have a case. Scoring 132.38 and losing is the kind of beat that makes you check the box score twice for a stat correction. Team Pillbert is still 6-3 with 93% playoff odds, but Luffy trimmed its title chances from 29% to 22%, the biggest drop in the league this week. Alan also cut Geno Smith and picked up Tyler Allgeier, which is about as quiet as a contender's waiver week gets.

No Banner only HULK put up the week's high score, 147.96, and flattened Ghostu-Spider SZN by 54. Kenneth Walker III went Gear 5 with 34.3 points, blowing past his 29-point top line, and Packers rookie Matthew Golden chipped in 27.4 on a 14.47 projection. The scary part for the rest of the league: D'Andre Swift scored 3.1 on a 17.2 projection, and Brucie still won by more than 50. At 7-2 with 1,203.9 points, he is the clear front-runner, with Luffy giving him a 33% shot at Buckaroo Bowl IV.

For Zoey, the pain was self-inflicted, and it came wearing green and gold. Jordan Love scored 36.18 on her bench while Jared Goff started and posted 5.3 on a 19.41 projection, which means the Wisconsin native benched the Packers quarterback in the one week he threw a party. The small mercy is the math: even with Love in the lineup, Ghostu-Spider SZN tops out around 124, still well short of HULK. Bijan Robinson did his part with 23.7, just under his top line, and Z² is now 3-6 on a two-game skid.

The Horse is Hea handled Counting or not Counting GV 104.88 to 87.94, though it wasn't the clean win the score suggests. JMoney got a Gear 5 from Joe Burrow, who scored 29.54 against a 27-point top line, but he also started Garrett Wilson, who did not play, and you don't beat anybody with a starter stuck at zero. Sonny got 26.5 from Bucky Irving and a so-so 7.8 from George Kittle, then left C.J. Stroud's 35.36 and Christian Watson's 26.6 on the bench in the same week he went out and picked up Patrick Mahomes. Sonny is 6-3; Jordan is 2-7, and Luffy now has his playoff chances at 0%.

Dawgs beat The fumblers 115.86 to 92.16, and the trade rematch had a twist: Randy's side of the deal actually won the week. Tee Higgins (17.7) and Jameson Williams (4.5) combined for 22.2 against 19.5 from Jonathan Taylor (6.9 on an 18.25 projection) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (12.6), and Mekhi won by 24 anyway. The real killer was Derrick Henry getting Seastoned with 5.6, under his 6-point bottom line, while Brock Bowers posted a steady 18.8 for Kai. Randy did find a waiver gem in Jonah Coleman (16.8) and kept churning with Tony Pollard and Rome Odunze, but The fumblers have now lost six straight and sit at 6% playoff odds.

The standings: HULK 7-2, Team Pillbert and The Horse is Hea at 6-3, Habibsters 5-4, Dawgs 4-5, The fumblers and Ghostu-Spider SZN at 3-6, and Counting or not Counting GV at 2-7. Luffy likes Habib more than his fourth-place seat suggests, with title odds jumping from 12% to 19%, now ahead of Sonny's 17%. Dawgs won and still saw their title odds halved from 12% to 6%, because winning doesn't help much when everyone above you keeps winning too.

Week 10 has real stakes. Habibsters take their four-game streak into a date with HULK, and Habib's playoff odds swing from 88% with a win to 71% with a loss. Dawgs host The Horse is Hea in Kai's biggest game of the year: 41% playoff odds with a win, 15% with a loss, while Sonny can push to 98%. The fumblers and Ghostu-Spider SZN meet in a de facto elimination game, with the loser falling to 1 or 2 percent. Team Pillbert gets Counting or not Counting GV and a chance to move to 97%.

social.author: Buckaroo Football League
social.text: Week 9 final: Habibsters 133.5, Team Pillbert 132.38. No Banner only HULK 147.96, Ghostu-Spider SZN 93.5. Dawgs 115.86, The fumblers 92.16. The Horse is Hea 104.88, Counting or not Counting GV 87.94. No Banner only HULK leads the league at 7-2.

social.author: Habibsters
social.text: FOUR STRAIGHT. Puka 28, CeeDee 28.5, and a 1.12-point finish we'll be telling our grandkids about. Player of the week is a tie and we refuse to pick. #HabibNation

social.author: Dana Whitfield
social.text: Garrett Wilson was listed as a starter for Counting or not Counting GV and did not play. One empty slot in a 17-point loss. Worth a lineup check before Sunday for anyone with questionable receivers.

social.author: Lambeau Lurker
social.text: Jordan Love: 36.18. Jordan Love's fantasy manager, who is FROM WISCONSIN: started Jared Goff. Somewhere a cheese factory just shut down in protest.

social.author: Gamma Ray Gang
social.text: Swift gives us 3.1 and we still win by 54. Walker went full Gear 5. Not even our bad players can lose us a game. 7-2. Get used to it.

social.author: Pillbert Til I Die
social.text: 132.38 points. A loss. By 1.12. I have watched the Puka touchdown 40 times hoping it turns into a field goal. Still 6-3. Still coming.

social.author: Fumble Recovery Unit
social.text: 3 AM update: our trade pieces outscored theirs 22.2 to 19.5 and we lost by 24. Henry gave us 5.6. Six straight. Jonah Coleman, you are the only one allowed to speak to me.

social.author: Horse Sense
social.text: Stroud 35 on the bench, Watson 26.6 on the bench, and we STILL won by 17. Imagine what happens when we start the right guys. 6-3 and the bench is scarier than most lineups.

social.author: Waiver Wire Whisperer
social.text: Habibsters were 1-4. Now Luffy has them ahead of The Horse is Hea in title odds. Ramon gets Habib next week and for the first time all year, I think HULK should be nervous.

trade_watch.take: Week one of the rematch goes to Randy on paper, as Higgins and Williams outscored Taylor and St. Brown 22.2 to 19.5. It still went down as a 24-point Dawgs win, so Kai keeps the trade and the scoreboard.

Javonte Williams added 20.4 and is now at 102.1 points for Philly, every one of them in the lineup. Stefon Diggs has 23.9 starting points for Randy. This one stopped being close weeks ago and keeps getting further apart.

Christian Watson scored 26.6 on Sonny's bench while Ashton Jeanty gave him 4.5 in the lineup, and James Cook III posted 16.7 for Kai. Mekhi has 33.8 starting points from this deal in two weeks and already flipped Williams for more; Sonny's side is looking thin.

Six weeks later, nobody has started anything from this deal. Chuba Hubbard has 85 points since, all of them for Philly after Sonny moved him on, and Rashee Rice has 22.2 on HULK's bench. The real winner is the guy who wasn't in it.

bios.1: Sonny is 6-3 and winning even when his best scores sit on the bench, as Stroud and Watson did this week. Luffy has him at 89% to make the playoffs and 17% for the title. A win over Dawgs would push him to 98%.
bios.2: Six straight losses have Randy at 3-6 with 6% playoff odds, despite Tee Higgins producing in his debut and Jonah Coleman delivering off the wire. He's been working the waiver wire hard, adding Pollard and Odunze. Next week against Ghostu-Spider SZN is effectively an elimination game.
bios.3: Jordan is 2-7 and Luffy has his playoff chances at 0%, even after another Gear 5 from Joe Burrow. Starting an inactive Garrett Wilson didn't help. From here, it's about playing spoiler, starting with Team Pillbert next week.
bios.4: Philly is 6-3 and still second, but a 132-point loss by 1.12 cost him the title-odds lead, dropping him from 29% to 22%. The playoff spot is close to secure at 93%. Counting or not Counting GV is next, and a win nearly locks it up.
bios.5: Mekhi has won two straight and got the better of the trade rematch with Randy, but sits at 4-5 with 28% playoff odds. A win over The Horse is Hea next week lifts that to 41%, while a loss drops it to 15%. Season on the line, in other words.
bios.6: Kaushal went from 1-4 to 5-4 with four straight wins, the latest a thriller over Team Pillbert. Luffy bumped his title odds to 19%, higher than two teams above him in the standings. Now comes the real test: first-place HULK.
bios.7: Ramon's juggernaut sits at 7-2 with a league-leading 1,203.9 points, and Luffy has it at 100% playoff odds and a league-best 33% to win Buckaroo Bowl IV. Even its off weeks from big names don't slow it down. Next up is the hottest team in the league.
bios.8: Zoe is 3-6 after a lopsided loss to HULK that included Jordan Love's 36 points on her bench. Bijan Robinson keeps showing up, but playoff odds are down to 6%. Beating The fumblers next week keeps her alive at 12%, and a loss all but ends it.
